## Make an activity your own

::: {.callout-note .example-author-notes}
### For course authors

Choose one example that fits your lesson. Open its source, copy it into your
Quarto page, and change the task and starting response. Keep the first attempt
small enough for students to discuss and revise.
:::

::: {.callout-note .example-author-notes}
### For course authors

Decide what you want students to notice. Should they explain a choice, fix a
mistake, or compare two methods? Try a plausible wrong answer yourself and
check that the feedback offers a useful next step.

[Follow the authoring guide](https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/ctm-assessment/blob/feature/scoped-policies/docs/authoring.md).
:::

::: {.callout-note .example-author-notes}
### Choose the kind of help

You can reuse the same feedback instructions across a course, then choose
different help for one page or one activity. In the mathematics tab, compare
a guiding question with a worked explanation of the same problem. Open the
source to see how each activity selects its instructions from a YAML file.
:::
